quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Stop your vehicle unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Let that car pass safely before you go.

questions.question: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at:

options.text: Curves and hills.
Churches and schools.
Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
Freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: You should increase the space between your car and the car ahead when:

options.text: A large vehicle is blocking your view.
You are leaving a freeway.
You are following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, when leaving a freeway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Cancels out the alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol level. While it may help you stay awake, it cannot make you sober or lower your blood alcohol.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Stay out of traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another car could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center. This means:

options.text: An intersection is coming up soon.
A construction area is ahead.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the road's edge. When this line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Before you start your car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers are buckled in.
Make sure only adult passengers are buckled in.
Make sure only child passengers are buckled in.
Make sure all passengers are buckled in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers are buckled in.
questions.explanation: Before you start your car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If a car is coming at you head-on in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and slow down.
Honk, steer right, and slow down.
Stay in your lane, honk, and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and slow down.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because if the other driver corrects, you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour slower reduces the impact.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Suggested speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are worse.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that you cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, you may pass if:

options.text: It is an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
There is no oncoming traffic.
You are at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, and the broken line is on your side, you may cross to pass only if no cars are coming toward you.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave more space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic moves, you have room to avoid a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also there.
Stop only if cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on state highways unless a different sign is posted?

options.text: 25 mph.
35 mph.
45 mph.
55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit on state highways is 55 mph unless a sign shows a different limit. Follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign shows:

options.text: A speed you can ignore in rain, snow, or ice.
A triangular shape.
Blue with black letters.
A recommended speed for curves and turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended speed for curves and turns.
questions.explanation: Signs for curves and turns show a recommended speed for that area. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, never go faster in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: You are driving when it starts to sleet or snow. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
Be careful when approaching other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow or sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one in front of you. Slippery roads need more distance to stop.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of both get weaker.
The effects of both get stronger.
It helps cure your illness.
It makes you a better driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both effects stronger. Driving after drinking alcohol or taking drugs is dangerous. Mixing them makes it even more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: It warns about current or possible dangers.
It tells you about school zones.
It tells you about parks and recreation areas.
It tells you where to find food and gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns about current or possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about dangers ahead. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign means you are coming up to a railroad crossing.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react slower to dangers on the road.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react slower to dangers on the road.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid crashes in icy or snowy conditions?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for traction.
Leave the highways as quickly as you can.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left on a multilane street or highway, start from the left lane.

questions.question: What must you do when turning right on a green light?

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What can help you avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn-out tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a layer of water between the tire and the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: Turns are not allowed on this road.
The road will narrow ahead.
Curves are coming up ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves are coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a winding road with three or more curves ahead.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming cars and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming cars and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay on the right when someone passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the other driver can move back into your lane easily.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not needed.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Follow what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and follow directions from crossing guards, signs, or police in school zones. Drive carefully around children at all times.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
Directs you to cities and towns.
Shows you traffic laws and rules.
Tells you about construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background. They alert you to conditions on or near the road.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even when you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign means an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid stopping suddenly.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop safely. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and helps avoid rear-end collisions.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. Before you move, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so they hear you.
Walk behind your car to make sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to make sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, especially when children are nearby, get out and check behind your vehicle. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop than on dry roads.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: You must follow a flagger's directions in construction zones. Slowing down and following their signals is required by law and keeps construction workers safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: T intersection.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a T intersection is coming. Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: A driver should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They're difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They're difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are harder to spot because they are smaller and may have less noticeable lighting. Many crashes happen because drivers looked but did not see them. Always watch for these smaller road users.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing where the crossing signals are flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When crossing signals flash, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for a lowered gate or listen for a train before crossing.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet roadway?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, faster speeds reduce your tire's grip. If you drive too fast, your tires will lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: To change lanes, signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement and onto the shoulder of the road, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drift off the pavement, reduce your speed without braking hard. Carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before getting behind the wheel:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have quicker reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.
